newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to up domestic sugar quota by 130,000 T.
newsitem.headline: Poland to up domestic sugar quota by 130,000 T.

text.p: The Polish Agriculture Ministry wants to raise the quota for domestic sugar sales by 130,000 tonnes to 1.63 million tonnes for the 1996/1997 growing season to help absorb this year's sugar surplus, a deputy minister said.

"The (Agriculture) minister applied for an increase in the A (domestic) quota this year by 130,000 tonnes...this would ease a bit the sugar surplus in the refineries and its price would slightly fall," Jerzy Pilarczyk told a news conference.
Agriculture Minister Roman Jagielinski, said the measure would be discussed at a cabinet meeting next Wednesday, November 27.
"Today I have agreed with Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz and (Finance Minister) Grzegorz Kolodko that the issue will be discussed during the next cabinet meeting," Jagielinski said.
Sugar output this year is expected to reach or exceed two million tonnes, 27 percent above last year's levels, due to increased growing area and higher sugar beet content.
The domestic sales quota was originally set at 1.5 million tonnes and the subsidised export quota was set at 122,500 tonnes this year and at 118,000 tonnes in 1997.
